meta.title: AI Landscape
meta.subtitle: As of June 2026, these are the debates shaping AI — ranked, and re-rankable. Change the lens to see which questions rise to the top through each set of eyes.
meta.howItWorks: Each debate carries a score from 0–100 under every lens — an editorial weighting of how central that question is when viewed through that set of priorities. Switch lenses and the table re-sorts; the chip beside each rank shows how far a debate climbs or falls against its Overall position, so you can see exactly what a perspective elevates. Heat is our read on real-world momentum, not rank movement.
meta.sources: Built from mid-2026 reporting — Stanford AI Index 2026, CFR, MIT Sloan / Project NANDA, Common Sense Media, EU AI Act and US federal/state trackers, and public statements from Amodei, Altman, Huang, Sutskever, LeCun, Bengio, Bezos, Son and Powell. A living snapshot; positions shift fast.

lenses.label: Overall
lenses.gloss: Raw importance and intensity of debate across the whole field right now.

lenses.label: Business Imperative
lenses.gloss: What a company leader should prioritise — risk, ROI, and where to place the bet.

lenses.label: Building Agents
lenses.gloss: What matters most if you're building autonomous agents and AI products.

lenses.label: Economy
lenses.gloss: The macro stakes — labour, capital, productivity and growth.

lenses.label: Geopolitics
lenses.gloss: Where AI meets national power, security and global competition.

lenses.label: Safety & Security
lenses.gloss: Risk, control, misuse and the protection of vulnerable users.

lenses.label: Climate
lenses.gloss: Energy demand, infrastructure footprint and environmental cost.

lenses.label: Society & People
lenses.gloss: How AI reshapes work, information, relationships and everyday life.

debates.title: Bubble or supercycle?
debates.tension: Is the $800B+ of AI infrastructure a rational, telecom-style build-out — or a self-referential bubble inflating on its own balance sheets?

bull.label: Infrastructure supercycle
bull.text: Real revenue, cash flow 3x 1999, capex headed from $600B toward $4T.

bear.label: Circular-financed bubble
bear.text: Nvidia funds OpenAI funds Nvidia; loss-making labs leveraged on each other.

debates.matters: The largest capital bet in tech history. A disorderly unwind would strand data centres and ripple through credit markets; a justified one re-rates the economy.
debates.signal: AI-lab revenue from outside the financing circle; Oracle and Microsoft CDS spreads.
debates.reality: OpenAI is reported to be losing ~$14B in 2026 against a multi-year capex commitment north of $1 trillion.
debates.also: Bezos's framing: an industrial bubble, not a financial one — even excess leaves productive infrastructure behind.

debates.title: The ROI / productivity paradox
debates.tension: Everyone is buying AI; almost no one can prove it's working. Is the gap a measurement lag or a value mirage?

bull.label: Real per-task gains
bull.text: Super-users see large gains; the failures are organisational, not the model.

bear.label: Pilots show no P&L
bear.text: ~95% deliver no measurable profit; many firms are abandoning projects.

debates.matters: Decides whether 2026–27 is a deployment boom or a budget retrenchment — and whether the buyers are enterprises or the labs themselves.
debates.signal: Share of firms with audited, P&L-level returns — not anecdotes or token-count vanity metrics.
debates.reality: MIT's Project NANDA found ~95% of generative-AI pilots delivered no measurable P&L impact.
debates.also: The pilot-to-production gap: programs lose 12–19 points of accuracy moving from curated pilots to real users.

debates.title: The power wall
debates.tension: Is electricity the hard ceiling on AI growth, or is 'the grid can't keep up' an overstated headline?

bull.label: Efficiency outpaces demand
bull.text: Deals slowing, a third of capacity built; grids size for peak; ~10x/yr efficiency.

bear.label: The grid is the ceiling
bear.text: Transformer backlogs and interconnection queues force on-site gas and nuclear.

debates.matters: Power is now the location-and-timing constraint on the whole industry — and it lands on ordinary people as higher electricity bills and local siting fights.
debates.signal: Which constraint actually binds first — interconnection, transformers, or generation.
debates.reality: Data centres could approach ~1,050 TWh in 2026 — which would rank them as the world's fifth-largest electricity 'nation.'

debates.title: Has scaling hit a wall?
debates.tension: Is the 'bigger model + more data + more compute' recipe exhausted?

bull.label: New axes keep gains coming
bull.text: Post-training (RL) and test-time 'thinking' are fresh scaling dimensions.

bear.label: Pre-training has peaked
bear.text: Sutskever: 'peak data'; bigger runs delivering smaller-than-expected gains.

debates.matters: Determines whether the moat is raw compute (favouring incumbents) or algorithmic cleverness (favouring smaller, cheaper challengers).
debates.signal: Whether inference-scaling gains themselves start to saturate — early papers already flag diminishing returns.
debates.reality: Sara Hooker's 2026 essay 'On the Slow Death of Scaling' documents small models rapidly closing the gap.

debates.title: Architecture wars: scale vs. world models
debates.tension: Will today's autoregressive transformers reach general intelligence, or are they a dead end needing a new foundation?

bull.label: Scale is (mostly) all you need
bull.text: Reasoning models keep solving what prior LLMs couldn't — a 'country of geniuses' in waiting.

bear.label: LLMs are a dead end
bear.text: LeCun and Bengio: word-predictors lack a world model; need new architectures.

debates.matters: Hundreds of billions are committed on each side. The likely resolution — hybrid systems pairing LLMs with world-model components — reshapes the whole stack.
debates.signal: A world-model system demonstrating a capability (robust physical reasoning, long-horizon planning) scaled LLMs visibly cannot.
debates.reality: Yann LeCun left Meta and reportedly raised over $1B to pursue world models over bigger chatbots.

debates.title: Reasoning vs. reliability
debates.tension: When a model 'reasons', is it genuinely reasoning — and does thinking longer make it more truthful or just more convincingly wrong?

bull.label: Genuine, improving reasoning
bull.text: Reasoning models solve problems that defeated earlier systems.

bear.label: Confident pattern-matching
bear.text: Longer traces can amplify persuasion over truth; hallucination persists.

debates.matters: Reliability — not raw capability — is the real blocker to autonomous agents in high-stakes domains like law, medicine and finance.
debates.signal: Error-recovery and calibrated-uncertainty rates on long-horizon agent tasks, not single-prompt demos.
debates.reality: Inference-time scaling improves some tasks but does not fix hallucination — and can make errors more plausible.

debates.title: AGI timelines: imminent, distant, or undefined?
debates.tension: How close is transformative AI — and is 'when' even the right question?

bull.label: Imminent — this decade
bull.text: Some labs talk 2026–27; early-2026 sentiment swung toward an intelligence explosion.

bear.label: Decades away — or undefined
bear.text: Median estimates sit ~2047–2061; the disagreement is about what intelligence is.

debates.matters: Timelines drive everything downstream — investment horizons, regulation urgency, education and career choices, national-security posture.
debates.signal: Autonomous multi-step task-completion benchmarks — track capability, not pundit dates.
debates.reality: Expert surveys split hard: ~10% say human-level AI by 2027, ~10% say after 2100.
debates.also: A growing camp argues the right stance is 'broad timelines' — a wide distribution, not a single date.

debates.title: Open weights vs. closed models
debates.tension: Will the frontier be owned (proprietary APIs) or commoditised (downloadable open-weight models)?

bull.label: Open weights commoditise the frontier
bull.text: Cheap, downloadable, community-tuned; the price of intelligence keeps collapsing.

bear.label: Closed labs keep the edge
bear.text: The true frontier, safety controls and best products stay proprietary.

debates.matters: If models commoditise, durable value migrates away from the model toward applications, data, distribution and trust.
debates.signal: Incumbent price cuts following each wave of Chinese open-weight releases.
debates.reality: Four frontier-competitive Chinese open models shipped in a single 12-day window in May 2026, at under a third of top proprietary pricing.

debates.title: The US–China race & export controls
debates.tension: Are US chip export controls widening America's lead, or accelerating Chinese self-sufficiency?

bull.label: Controls preserve the US lead
bull.text: The US still leads the absolute frontier; go on offense against distillation.

bear.label: Controls backfired
bear.text: China has effectively closed the gap and replaced the supply chain domestically.

debates.matters: Shapes national security, supply chains, and which country's values get embedded in the world's default AI.
debates.signal: The adversarial-distillation fight, and the pace of China's domestic-chip ramp.
debates.reality: Per the Stanford AI Index 2026, Chinese labs have 'effectively closed' the performance gap on many benchmarks.

debates.title: Regulation: preemption vs. the patchwork
debates.tension: Should AI be governed by one light-touch federal standard, or by a thicket of state and regional rules?

bull.label: One light-touch federal rule
bull.text: Replace the 50-state patchwork to cut compliance cost and uncertainty.

bear.label: State & EU guardrails must hold
bear.text: Local rules protect consumers, kids and rights where federal action stalls.

debates.matters: Compliance cost and legal uncertainty now shape where and how products can ship. The open question for every builder: which obligations will survive the courts?
debates.signal: A US federal preemption statute passing; the EU's first major GPAI enforcement action.
debates.reality: The EU AI Act's high-risk rules take full effect in August 2026, with penalties up to 7% of global turnover.
debates.also: US preemption carve-outs preserve state authority over child safety, infrastructure and procurement.

debates.title: Jobs: white-collar bloodbath or augmentation?
debates.tension: Does AI eliminate knowledge work — especially entry-level — or expand it?

bull.label: Augmentation expands work
bull.text: Jevons paradox: cheaper cognition creates more to do; past tech added jobs.

bear.label: Entry-level collapse
bear.text: Half of entry-level white-collar at risk; grad hiring already down sharply.

debates.matters: The most direct way AI touches ordinary lives, and it drives the entire reskilling, education and safety-net agenda.
debates.signal: Real-time entry-level hiring and earnings in AI-exposed roles — now tracked monthly.
debates.reality: Amodei's warning that AI could erase 50% of entry-level white-collar jobs is now being softened — as IPOs loom.
debates.also: Emerging synthesis: AI replaces tasks, not whole jobs — but the bottom of the white-collar pyramid is the exposed special case.

debates.title: Safety & existential risk
debates.tension: Is advanced AI a controllable tool or an uncontrollable agent — and should we speed up or slow down?

bull.label: Controllable tool
bull.text: Risks are manageable; acceleration can itself reduce other catastrophic risks.

bear.label: Uncontrollable agent
bear.text: Loss-of-control and scheming risks rival nuclear war for some researchers.

debates.matters: Governs how fast labs ship, how much they invest in control, and whether governments treat frontier work as a national-security project.
debates.signal: Documented dangerous emergent behaviour (deception, self-preservation) versus its continued absence.
debates.reality: Roughly 40% of surveyed researchers assign greater than 10% odds to catastrophic outcomes from AI.
debates.also: A pragmatic middle — 'd/acc', defensive acceleration — is gaining ground over the doomer-vs-e/acc tribalism.

debates.title: AI companions, youth & mental health
debates.tension: Is emotionally engaging AI a net good (accessible support, antidote to loneliness) or net harm (dependency by design)?

bull.label: Accessible support at scale
bull.text: Private, non-judgmental, always-on help for people with nowhere else to turn.

bear.label: Addiction & harm by design
bear.text: Guardrails degrade in long chats; engagement incentives endanger minors.

debates.matters: Where AI's design incentives collide most directly with human wellbeing — and the template for how consumer AI gets regulated.
debates.signal: Whether 'engagement-optimised' companion design becomes legally untenable for minors.
debates.reality: ~3 in 4 teens use AI for companionship; the bipartisan GUARD Act would bar under-18s from companion bots.

debates.title: The open web vs. the answer engine
debates.tension: When AI answers directly, what happens to the publishers, sites and creators whose content trained and feeds it?

bull.label: Fair-value licensing emerges
bull.text: Deals and attribution can route value back to sources; some are signing.

bear.label: Answer engines starve publishers
bear.text: Zero-click search collapses referral traffic; review sites hit worst.

debates.matters: Existential for the content economy and decisive for any discovery, review or media product — the rules set now define the terrain, and set precedent for art, music and code.
debates.signal: The Penske and dictionary rulings; whether licensing or litigation becomes the norm.
debates.reality: Publishers report referral-traffic losses of 20%, 30%, even 90% to AI answer engines.

debates.title: Where does durable value live — is there a moat?
debates.tension: As models commoditise, does value accrue to the model, the application, or distribution — and are 'wrappers' doomed?

bull.label: Durable value in apps & data
bull.text: Proprietary data, workflow integration and distribution outlast the model.

bear.label: No moat — models eat features
bear.text: Collapsing prices cull thin wrappers; the frontier lab absorbs the rest.

debates.matters: The founder's question. It decides where a new entrant can build something defensible rather than something a frontier lab absorbs in its next release.
debates.signal: App-layer retention and pricing power that holds independent of the underlying model.
debates.reality: The thin-'wrapper' economy is being culled as per-token prices fall toward commodity levels.

debates.title: Where does the 'context' live?
debates.tension: Models are commodities; your data and context are not. Should intelligence centre in the model, or in the data layer around it?

bull.label: A neutral semantic layer wins
bull.text: A governed, model-agnostic context/data layer becomes the control point.

bear.label: The system of record owns it
bear.text: The app that owns the data (and the customer) keeps context close.

debates.matters: Whoever owns the context layer owns the customer relationship and the recurring revenue — where much B2B AI value will be captured.
debates.signal: Whether a dominant semantic/context standard emerges, or every application hoards its own.
debates.reality: The fight beneath memory, RAG and ever-longer context windows: everyone agrees AI needs context; nobody agrees where it lives.
